Maya: Heads-up: noticed ~12% P99 increase on a few production pods after the recent kernel-pick tweak. Only on machines with SM 8.6 + driver 537.
Alex: ugh, thanks. which tweak specifically?
Maya: We tightened the fp16->bf16 fastpath gate to prefer TC kernels for seqlen<=64. Seems on some cards the bf16 TC kernel falls back to a slower path at runtime. Logs show fallback from kernel 'tc_bf16_fast' -> 'matmul_fallback'.
Alex: that matches one change in main: lowered tensorcore-confidence threshold from 0.85 -> 0.7 to favor TC kernels more aggressively. Could be a mis-detect for bf16 support.
Jin: paste of microbench on an affected node: ```bash
# run microbench
./nvbench --kernel tc_bf16_fast --seqlen 32 --iters 200
# output excerpt
median: 0.82ms
fallbacks: 34/200 -> avg 1.9ms
```
Maya: fallback count is the smoking gun. KV cache pressure increased too — we saw more prefetch misses during fallback bursts, which amplifies latency.
Sam: do we rely on driver version heuristics anywhere? last I checked we used a combo: SM >= 86 && driver major >= 537 -> allow bf16 TC.
Alex: yes, current capability probe uses driver + reported device attributes, but sometimes the runtime-level PTX query returns inconsistent answers right after process start. Could be a race with CUDA context init.
perf-bot: profile summary attached: p99 increased 11.8% after roll (2026-03-15 03:12 UTC), correlates with a jump in kernel fallback events (+410%).
Maya: repro steps I used: start server with --autotune=on, send steady qps with seqlen=32, then enable perf tracing. Attaching snippet of the trace where we see kernel pick then fallback: ```
[KERNEL_PICK] tc_bf16_fast (cap_flags=SM86,TC_OK,BF16_QUIRK=maybe)
[KERNEL_LAUNCH] returned KERNEL_FALLBACK_REASON=unsupported_math
```
Jin: idea: extend the start-up capability probe to run a short microkernel test (tiny matmul) on a reserved stream to verify actual BF16/TC behavior instead of trusting reported caps. If it fails, mark TC as disabled for this process instance.
Sam: +1. That avoids relying on driver strings. We should keep the probe lightweight (<10ms) and run only once per worker.
Alex: also we can add a dynamic-circuit-breaker: if fallback_rate > 1% over the last 60s for that worker/variant, temporarily bias away from TC kernels for same seqlen bucket. Fast recovery if error goes away.
Maya: sounds good. We should also check batching heuristics: when fallback spikes we see batching collapse (smaller, less efficient batches). Might be worth emitting a metric `kernel_fallback_longevity` to catch when fallbacks are sustained.
perf-bot: created perf ticket #INF-9274 with logs and sample node IDs.
Jin: I'll prototype a microprobe in runtime bootstrap and add a Prom counter for fallback events. Plan: PR with opt-in flag first.
Maya: thanks. can we also add a small unit test in arch-detect that simulates race conditions (delayed PTX query) so we avoid flakey detection?
Alex: agree. I'll sketch the dynamic circuit-breaker policy and threshold math.
Sam: ping me on the PR for release notes — need to mention behavior change for Dedicated nodes.
Maya: thanks team. I can roll a canary tomorrow once Jin's probe is in opt-in. :thumbsup:
